title: How to Build a Retirement Plan When You Expect Periodic Windfalls (bonuses, inheritance)
description: Managing 'Lumpy' capital infusions without lifestyle creep.
content:
Some financial lives are linear (salary); others are lumpy (bonuses, commissions, inheritances). If your wealth comes in chunks, standard 'monthly budget' advice fails. The danger of windfalls is 'Mental Accounting'—treating the lump sum as 'Play Money' while ignoring the deficit in your daily retirement funding. To succeed, you must treat windfalls as your primary funding source for retirement, allowing your daily salary to simply cover daily bills.

Key Takeaways

  • The 'Zero-Based' Bonus: Commit 100% of every windfall to long-term goals before it hits your account. If you get a $20,000 bonus, $0 should go to checking; $20,000 goes to Brokerage/Debt.
  • Lump Sum Investing: Mathematically, investing a lump sum immediately beats dollar-cost averaging 66% of the time. When the windfall hits, buy the market that day. Don't let it sit in cash.
  • The 'Tax Trap': Windfalls (Inheritance/Bonuses) often come with tax bills. Inherited IRAs have RMDs. Bonuses have withholding. Always reserve 30% for the IRS before spending a dime.
  • Lifestyle Cap: Do not upgrade your recurring expenses (Car/House) based on irregular income. If the bonuses stop, you still have the mortgage. Keep fixed costs tied to base salary only.

Why It Matters (US Context)

The 'Inherited IRA 10-Year Rule' requires non-spouse heirs to drain the account within 10 years. This creates a 'forced income' stream that can spike your tax bracket. Strategic planning is needed to minimize the tax hit.

The Allocation Waterfall

You receive a $50,000 windfall. Where does it go?

Bucket 1: The Past (Debt)

Priority: Extreme.
Action: Pay off all consumer debt immediately. If you have student loans >6%, kill them.
Result: You lower your monthly burn rate instantly.

Bucket 2: The Future (Retirement)

Priority: High.
Action: Max out Roth IRAs for you and spouse ($14k). Max HSA ($8.3k). Put the rest in Taxable Brokerage.
Result: One windfall can fund 3 years of retirement contributions.

Bucket 3: The Present (Fun)

Priority: Low.
Action: Take 5-10% off the top for a guilt-free splurge.
Result: Prevents deprivation fatigue.

Managing Volatility

  1. Super-Fund 529s: You can put 5 years of contributions ($90k) into a 529 at once (Superfunding). This is the best use of a massive inheritance.
  2. The 'Opportunity Fund': Keep a portion of the windfall in liquid T-Bills. When the market crashes or a real estate deal pops up, you have the 'Dry Powder' to act.
  3. Estate Taxes: If inheriting >$13M (Federal) or less in some states (MA/WA/OR), estate taxes apply. You might receive less than you think. Don't spend it before probate closes.
  4. Don't Quit Your Job: A windfall of $500k is not 'Retire Now' money. It is 'Retire 10 Years Earlier' money. Let it compound. Don't eat the seed corn.

Frequently Asked Questions

Should I pay off my mortgage?

If it helps you sleep, yes. But investing the windfall often yields more. It's a choice between 'Optimization' (Investing) and 'Peace' (Payoff).

Is inheritance taxable?

Usually no (income tax free). But IRAs/401ks you inherit ARE taxable when withdrawn. Know the difference between 'Cash' and 'Pre-Tax Assets'.

What if the windfall is stock?

You get a 'Step-Up in Basis'. You can sell the stock tax-free immediately. Diversify it into an Index Fund. Don't hold a concentrated position just because Mom loved GE.
